source.title: Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video
source.authors: Jaedong Hwang; Xiaoqian Shen; Er-Nie Chang; Changsheng Zhao; Chong Zhou; Saksham Suri; Qi Qian; Ze-Chun Liu; Le-Meng Wu; Qin-Si Wang; Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi; Wei Wen

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates downstream benchmark performance at multiple amounts of video mid-training, bearing on V6, but does not use the original parameter/data/compute scaling-law measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper cites neural scaling laws as motivation but does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit scaling laws. Its endpoint comparisons between video mid-training and no mid-training, and between caption and visual-token objectives, do not by themselves test a scaling law; the reported training-stage trajectory is included for V6.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Kaplan and Hoffmann scaling laws only as motivation. It fits no power law, measures no held-out pretraining loss, and varies neither parameters nor compute. Its only training-amount result is three intermediate checkpoints (0.3, 0.5, 1.0 epochs) from one cosine-schedule video mid-training run of one 1.7B model, each followed by instruction tuning. This measures when a mid-training stage's benefit appears, not whether downstream performance scales predictably with model scale or pretraining loss. Intermediate cosine-schedule checkpoints also do not stand in for separately trained data budgets. So it does not test V6 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but incomplete. The authors' main conclusions are three. First, raw-video next-visual-token mid-training of Qwen3-1.7B raises video (+2.9) and image (+5.1) benchmark averages after identical instruction tuning. Second, it preserves text (48.9 vs 48.0). Third, caption-prediction targets give no advantage. The early-gain-then-plateau trajectory (gains within 0.3 epochs, <0.5-point change afterwards) is a secondary analysis. The authors leave denser sampling, frame-shuffling controls and larger models to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study mid-trains one pretrained language model on continuous raw-video features and measures downstream benchmark trajectories; it does not reproduce the original language-model loss-scaling or compute-allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-stage amount: image and video gains appear early and then plateau.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen3-1.7B, video mid-training gains on image (+4.9) and video (+3.1) benchmarks appear by 19.5B visual tokens (0.3 epoch). They then vary <0.5 points through 64.4B tokens; text stays within 0.9 points of baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream benefit of continued self-supervised video mid-training saturates early in visual-token count for a small LM (checkpoint trajectory within one schedule, with instruction tuning at each checkpoint).

record.problems: Only one language-model size is studied, and no pretraining-loss scaling fit, parameter sweep, compute-optimal allocation, or uncertainty estimates are reported. Downstream checkpoints are each followed by instruction tuning.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on V6 were left out. Endpoint benchmark comparisons and caption-objective ablations were not recorded because they do not measure downstream performance as a function of training scale.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power law in parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fit used to predict larger runs.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Video mid-training is used, but no power-law form is fitted or tested in video or transfer.
No variation in model scale, no pretraining-loss predictor, and no fitted downstream relation. There are only three checkpoints of one run.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits compared.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' for V6 is overturned. The checkpoint trajectory is not a scaling-law test: there is one model size, no fit, intermediate checkpoints of a single cosine run, and SFT at each checkpoint. It is a different regime (multimodal mid-training). The record's own labels said the result was 'not a fitted or demonstrated general prediction rule', which is consistent with not testing. No instructions in text.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or optimal parameter/token scaling is tested.
No comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count is reported.
Video is used as a training regime, but the paper does not test whether power-law forms hold in video or other modalities, or under repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.

The study tracks downstream benchmark averages over video mid-training tokens for one model size; it does not test prediction from pretraining loss, larger model scales, or a fitted downstream scaling relationship.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits are compared across counting, schedule, data, or fitting choices.

relation.reason: Kaplan and Hoffmann scaling laws motivate seeking additional training modalities in the introduction; the experiments do not evaluate or apply those laws.

tranche.reason: The study compares mid-training objectives and reports downstream trajectories from one model's training run. It neither tests a scaling-law form or predictive relation nor uses a scaling law as a tool.

source_check.notes: The trajectories use checkpoints from one cosine-schedule run, each followed by instruction tuning; they establish early gains and a plateau without a scaling fit. Table 4 resolves the displaced image-average entries in the extracted Table 2.
